mq-03-monte.context: Micah announces a future in which the mountain of the Lord's house will be exalted. Nations and peoples go up to it not to wage war, but to learn God's ways.
mq-03-monte.focusQuestion: What do you need to learn from God before seeking peace your own way?
mq-03-monte.keywordGloss: The mountain of the Lord's house is the place from which instruction and the word go out to the nations.
facts: The mountain of the Lord's house will be established as the highest of the mountains.
The peoples will stream to the mountain of the Lord's house.
Many nations invite one another to go up to the mountain of the Lord.
The nations want to learn God's ways and walk in his paths.
Swords will become plowshares, and spears will become pruning hooks.
Each one will sit under their own vine and fig tree, without fear.

mq-04-belem.context: In a time of siege, when Israel's judge is humiliated, Micah announces that the ruler will come from Bethlehem. He will care for the people in the strength of the Lord and bring security.
mq-04-belem.focusQuestion: In what area of your life do you need to trust God's care today?
mq-04-belem.keywordGloss: A small town in Judah from which comes the ruler who cares for the people in the strength of the Lord.
reflectionPrompts: He will care in the Lord's strength
facts: A siege will be laid, and they will strike the judge of Israel on the cheek with a rod.
From Bethlehem will come the one who is to rule in Israel.
After the birth, the rest of the brothers will return to the people of Israel.
The ruler will care for the people in the strength of the Lord and in the majesty of his name.
The people will live securely because the ruler will be great to the ends of the earth.
Seven shepherds and eight princes will be raised up against Assyria.

mq-05-mar.context: Near the end of the book, after announcements of judgment, Micah celebrates the incomparable God: he forgives, does not hold on to his anger forever, and casts sins into the depths of the sea.
mq-05-mar.focusQuestion: What sin do you need to let God cast far away, without fishing it back out?
mq-05-mar.keywordGloss: God delights in showing faithful kindness, forgiving instead of holding on to anger forever.
reflectionPrompts: Sins at the bottom of the sea
facts: God will show wonders as in the days of the exodus from Egypt.
God pardons iniquity and forgets the transgression of the remnant of his inheritance.
God does not hold on to his anger forever.
God delights in showing mercy.
God will tread down iniquities and cast sins into the depths of the sea.
God will show faithfulness to Jacob and mercy to Abraham, as he promised the fathers.

miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senhor-requer-de-.context: God reminds the people of his righteous acts in the past. Then come questions about how to come before him, with ever-bigger offerings, until the clear answer of what he requires.
miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senhor-requer-de-.focusQuestion: How can you practice justice and mercy in a choice this week?
miqueias-miqueias-01-o-senhor-requer-de-.keywordGloss: Loving mercy is valuing goodness and forgiveness in how you treat people, as God asks.
facts: God calls the people to remember his righteous acts from Shittim to Gilgal.
The person asks what to bring before the Lord and whether to come with burnt offerings.
The question exaggerates, imagining thousands of rams and ten thousand rivers of oil.
The Lord requires doing justice, loving mercy and walking humbly with God.
God denounces treasures of wickedness and the short measure in the house of the wicked.

miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-efrata.context: After the questions about offerings in Micah 6, this scene looks at the promise of Micah 5: from Bethlehem, small in Judah, will come the one who will rule in Israel.
miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-efrata.focusQuestion: Where have you judged something too small for God to act?
miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-efrata.keywordGloss: Small town in Judah from which, according to the promise, the ruler of Israel will come.
facts: Bethlehem is too small to be counted among the thousands of Judah.
From Bethlehem will come the one who will rule in Israel.
The ruler's origins are from ancient times, from eternity.
The Lord requires justice, mercy and walking humbly with God.
The person asks whether to come to the Lord with burnt offerings and year-old calves.

miqueias-miqueias-03-desafio-miqueias.context: This challenge reviews Micah 4, 5 and 7: nations learning on the mountain, a ruler coming from Bethlehem, and God who in the end forgives and casts sins into the depths of the sea.
miqueias-miqueias-03-desafio-miqueias.focusQuestion: Which of these three scenes most challenges your trust in God today?
miqueias-miqueias-03-desafio-miqueias.keywordGloss: God's faithful kindness: he teaches the nations, raises up the ruler and forgives his people at the end of the book.
reflectionPrompts: Receiving forgiveness, sins cast into the sea
facts: Many nations go up the mountain to learn God's ways.
Swords will become plowshares and spears will become pruning hooks.
From Bethlehem will come the one who will rule in Israel.
The ruler will care for the people in the strength of the Lord.
God does not keep his anger forever, because he delights in mercy.
God will cast all sins into the depths of the sea.
